eligibility.quote: The problem was that serial.block() is called before serial.open() in hydro branch kobuki_driver/kobuki.cpp line 93

failed_conditions.quote:
In the version 0.3.9, which I confirmed that working fine,  the block() was called after open().

The description of open() in ecl_core/ecl_device/serial_pos.hpp:line 153 tells that block() needs to be called after serial is opened.

loudness.quote: Same result though - terminal get's unresponsive.

resolution.quote: Thus, the proposed patch is going to call serial.block() function after serial.open() in kobuki.cpp

notes:
Independently re-decided and agree. E1: issue 272 body ('And prevents Ctrl+C to work.
Strange thing is that it happens only sometimes.') with maintainer log excerpts (bit-pirate: 'I have a new version of mangled output - this time all is CAPTIAL LETTERS! :-)') and the root-cause diagnosis by maintainer jihoonl (2013-08-01) plus fix PR #278. E2 stop 6: ecl_devices (ecl::Serial, stonier/ecl_core) and kobuki_driver are separately released packages -- kobuki_driver/package.xml at ba100858 declares '<build_depend>ecl_devices</build_depend>' and '<run_depend>ecl_devices</run_depend>' (read at raw.githubusercontent.com/yujinrobot/kobuki/ba100858672f90cc249ac18513541905a7c7a104/kobuki_driver/package.xml, lines 19 and 27); the failure is a wrong call ORDER crossing the library boundary against the provider's documented precondition -- the tree explicitly lists 'component order' among the interface-crossing wrongs -- verified directly in the provider at 0.60.5: serial_pos.hpp open() documentation 'If successful, it will configure the port with a blocking policy and a
     * timeout of 5s. Use the block() method after opening to alter the behaviour.' and serial_pos.cpp line 320 'tcsetattr(file_descriptor, TCSAFLUSH, &options);' inside block(); the consumer side at ba100858 kobuki.cpp line 93 'serial.block(4000); // blocks by default, but just to be clear!' before line 95 'serial.open(parameters.device_port, ...)' (read in the raw file); steps 3-5 do not stop (fix is a C++ source reorder in the consumer). Condition class 'other' agree (documented call-order precondition; no dedicated class); implicated elements api:ecl::Serial::block + api:ecl::Serial::open agree. E3 PAIR agree (maintainer: 'In the version 0.3.9, which I confirmed that working fine,  the block() was called after open().' -- the provider is unchanged in the relevant respect, the consumer's ordering changed). E4 agree. Loudness silent_documented agree: no diagnostic from either side; the provider's silence is itself noted by the maintainer ('Also, ecl serial.block() should warn user if file_descriptor is not initialized.'); detection_stage activate -- agree, with the same caveat the spec records (the misuse runs in Kobuki::init during start-up, before the driver's run loop; a reader reserving 'activate' for lifecycle transitions would say 'run'); this does not change the loudness verdict. Resolution recommended agree: the fix is merged (commit 054c753, verified: moves 'serial.block(4000);' after 'is_connected = true;' inside the try in Kobuki::init and adds it after the reconnect serial.open() in Kobuki::spin) but the thread closes without showing the terminal problem gone; the 0.3.9 'working fine' statement is an observation with the older consumer release, not with the fix.
